reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs, nanoribbons, strain gradients from lateral confinement, magnetocaloric entropy changes, or thermal lag effects. E1 describes bulk magnetic measurements and domain imaging on unspecified materials, while E2 discusses coercivity in CoCrFeNi films related to microcracks and grain size, not thermal transport. None of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Lateral confinement in nanoribbons induces strain gradients that modify magnetic domain configurations.
Modified domain configurations shift, broaden the magnetocaloric entropy change peak, and enhance hysteresis.
Limited heat transfer in as-deposited structures causes a thermal lag that further broadens the response and increases hysteretic losses.
An ultrathin high-thermal-conductivity interfacial layer can reduce this extrinsic thermal lag.
Reducing thermal lag sharpens the magnetocaloric transition and reduces hysteresis.
